name: Media
description: Image pipeline and gallery editor: upload limits, downscaling, thumbnails, WebP. Other modules attach galleries to their entities through it.

settings.label: Max file size, MB
settings.help: Rejects bigger uploads. 0 = no limit (PHP's upload_max_filesize still applies).

settings.label: Max dimension, px
settings.help: Longer side of the stored original is downscaled to this. 0 = keep as uploaded.

settings.label: Store the original untouched
settings.help: Keeps the uploaded file byte-for-byte in its own format with no recompression. Overrides the max-dimension limit above.

settings.label: Original re-encode quality
settings.help: 1–100, used only when an original actually gets downscaled.

settings.label: Thumbnail sizes
settings.help: Comma-separated WxH. The storefront asks for a width and gets the smallest size at least that wide: 120 in the cart and the image strip, 400 on catalogue cards, 800 on the product page. Removing a size these ask for means they fall back to the full original.

options.contain: Contain — fit inside, keep the whole image
options.cover: Cover — fill the box, crop the overflow
options.pad: Pad — fit inside, then pad to the exact box

settings.label: How to fit the box
settings.help: Contain never loses pixels but gives thumbnails of differing shapes. Cover makes every thumbnail exactly the box, at the price of cutting edges off tall or wide photos. Pad also makes them identical, without cutting anything, by adding background — the safe choice for a catalogue grid.

settings.label: Padding colour
settings.help: Used by the Pad mode only. A hex colour, e.g. #ffffff.

settings.label: Trim uniform borders on upload
settings.help: Photos exported from a studio often carry wide empty margins, which make the subject look small in a fixed box. This crops that border away from the stored original, so every thumbnail inherits it. It changes the stored file and cannot be undone by rebuilding thumbnails — only by re-uploading.

settings.label: Trim tolerance, %
settings.help: How far a pixel may differ from the corner colour and still count as background. 0 trims only a perfectly flat border; 6 copes with JPEG noise and soft shadows; too high starts eating the product.

settings.label: Convert images inside text to WebP
settings.help: Off by default, and the reasoning is the opposite of the thumbnails above. A thumbnail is generated in several sizes and served a million times, so WebP wins outright. An image inside a description is stored once and served as it is — and for a screenshot full of small text, or a PNG with transparency, the re-encode is sometimes visibly worse than what was uploaded. Which of those your shop mostly uploads is not something the engine can know. Animated GIFs are never converted whatever this says: it would keep the first frame and throw the animation away.

settings.label: JPEG/PNG thumbnail quality
settings.help: 1–100, used when WebP thumbnails are off.

settings.label: Rebuild all thumbnails
settings.help: Existing images keep the thumbnails they were uploaded with. Save the settings above first, then run this to apply the new sizes and format to everything already in the catalogue.
